cases.translation: Tikhonov drank some juniper vodka, grunted and grew sad.
cases.explain: After «выпить» meaning to drink some of something, the substance goes into the partitive genitive: выпил можжевеловой.

cases.sentence: Я с самого начала был ___ этой авантюры.
cases.translation: From the very beginning I was an opponent of this escapade.
cases.explain: A predicate noun after past-tense «был» stands in the instrumental, so противник becomes противником.

cases.sentence: Революция достигает чего-нибудь нужного, если совершается в ___, а не на стогнах.
cases.translation: A revolution achieves anything worthwhile only if it takes place in hearts and not in the public squares.
cases.explain: «В» answering «где?» (location, not direction) takes the prepositional; the plural of сердце there is сердцах.

cases.sentence: Тихонов прибил к ___ елисейковского сельсовета свои четырнадцать тезисов.
cases.translation: Tikhonov nailed his fourteen theses to the gates of the Yeliseykovo village soviet.
cases.explain: The preposition «к» (towards, onto) always governs the dative; ворота is plural-only, so the dative is воротам.

cases.sentence: Тихонов прибил к воротам елисейковского сельсовета свои четырнадцать ___.
cases.translation: Tikhonov nailed his fourteen theses to the gates of the Yeliseykovo village soviet.
cases.explain: Numerals from five upwards — including четырнадцать — require the genitive plural of the counted noun: четырнадцать тезисов.

cases.translation: That password was mischievous and ambiguous.
cases.explain: Пароль is the subject of the sentence (the short adjectives шаловлив and двусмыслен describe it), so it stands in the nominative.

cases.sentence: Одно письмо было адресовано ___ Норвегии Улафу.
cases.translation: One letter was addressed to Olav, the King of Norway.
cases.explain: The addressee of «адресовать» is the recipient, and recipients take the dative: адресовано королю.
«В» with a stretch of time answering «когда?» takes the accusative: в эту ночь.

reading.question: What does Tikhonov say he is doing when Venichka finds him in the jasmine bushes?
reading.explain: He says everything has long been ready for the rising except the theses, and now the theses are ready too.

reading.ru: Тихонов выпил можжевеловой, крякнул и загрустил.
reading.question: How does Tikhonov react each time Venichka offers him juniper vodka?
options: He drinks, grunts and turns sad
He becomes cheerful and starts singing
reading.correct: He drinks, grunts and turns sad
reading.explain: Both rounds of juniper vodka end the same way: he drinks and grows sad again.

reading.ru: Да. В девять ноль-ноль по Гринвичу.
reading.question: At what hour were the rebels to gather?
options: At nine o'clock sharp, Greenwich time
At dawn, before the shops opened
At midnight by the cattle yard
reading.correct: At nine o'clock sharp, Greenwich time
reading.explain: The appointed time, repeated twice at the parting, is nine hundred hours Greenwich time.

reading.question: What does Venichka tell his comrade to do before the rising?
options: To try to get some sleep that night
reading.correct: To try to get some sleep that night
reading.explain: They part with the wish that Tikhonov manage to sleep, and Tikhonov promises he will.

reading.ru: Я с самого начала говорил, что революция достигает чего-нибудь нужного, если совершается в сердцах, а не на стогнах.
reading.question: Where does Venichka claim a revolution must take place if it is to achieve anything?
options: In people's hearts, not in the public squares
In the capital, not in the provinces
At the cattle yard, not in the village
In the shops, not on the roads
reading.correct: In people's hearts, not in the public squares
reading.explain: He insists he said from the start that only a revolution in hearts achieves anything worthwhile.

reading.ru: Но уж раз начали без меня – я не мог быть в стороне от тех, кто начал.
reading.question: Why does Venichka take part in the uprising although he opposed it?
options: Because it had been started without him and he could not stand aside
Because he had drafted the theses himself
Because he was promised a post in the new capital
Because he was afraid of Tikhonov
reading.correct: Because it had been started without him and he could not stand aside
reading.explain: Having called the venture barren as a fig tree, he still joins, hoping to soften the bloodshed.

reading.ru: В девятом часу по Гринвичу, в траве у скотного двора, мы сидели и ждали.
reading.question: Where do the conspirators wait for the appointed hour?
options: In the grass by the cattle yard
Behind the gates of the village soviet
reading.correct: In the grass by the cattle yard
reading.explain: They sit in the grass by the cattle yard, greeting each newcomer with the password.

reading.ru: Все началось с того, что Тихонов прибил к воротам елисейковского сельсовета свои четырнадцать тезисов.
reading.question: How is the beginning of the whole affair first described?
options: Tikhonov nailed fourteen theses to the gates of the village soviet
Tikhonov sent a telegram to Norway
Tikhonov was arrested at the cattle yard
Tikhonov gave a speech at the shop in Polomy
reading.correct: Tikhonov nailed fourteen theses to the gates of the village soviet
reading.explain: This Luther-like gesture is given as the starting point of the rising.

reading.ru: Вернее, не прибил к воротам, а написал на заборе мелом, и это скорее были слова, а не тезисы, четкие и лапидарные слова, а не тезисы, и было их всего два, а не четырнадцать, – но, как бы то ни было, с этого все началось.
reading.question: How does the narrator immediately correct that account?
options: It was two words chalked on a fence, not fourteen theses nailed to gates
It was fourteen theses, but posted in Cherkasovo
It was a speech, not a written text
It was written by Venichka, not by Tikhonov
reading.correct: It was two words chalked on a fence, not fourteen theses nailed to gates
reading.explain: He takes the grand version apart word by word, leaving two blunt words in chalk.

reading.question: What happens to Yeliseykovo during the advance?
options: It is bombed by the Norwegians
reading.explain: The two columns march unhindered, and Yeliseykovo falls.

reading.ru: Черкасово валялось у нас в ногах, Неугодово и Пекша молили о пощаде.
reading.question: Which villages are said to have begged for mercy?
reading.explain: Cherkasovo grovels at their feet while Neugodovo and Peksha plead for mercy.

reading.question: What does the thoroughly drunk Tikhonov shout that they need?
reading.explain: Venichka calls him a brilliant theoretician but useless in practice for this outburst.

reading.ru: Все четыре открытки были очень красивые, с виньеточками и желудями.
reading.question: What is said about the four postcards the rebels sent?
options: They were very pretty, with little vignettes and acorns
reading.correct: They were very pretty, with little vignettes and acorns
reading.explain: The hope is that the recipients will be pleased and recognise the rebels as subjects of international law.

reading.ru: Никто в эту ночь не спал.
reading.question: How do the rebels spend the night after the congress?
options: Awake, staring at the sky and waiting for bombs and intervention
Asleep in the barns of Cherkasovo
reading.correct: Awake, staring at the sky and waiting for bombs and intervention
reading.explain: Enthusiasm keeps them all up, waiting for Norwegian bombs, the opening of the shops and the intervention.

reading.ru: Не спал и пленный, бывший предсельсовета Анатолий Иваныч, он выл из своего сарая, как тоскующий пес.
reading.question: What worries the captured Anatoly Ivanych in his shed?
options: That nobody will bring him a drink in the morning
That he will be shot at dawn
That his village has been renamed
That the Norwegians will bomb the shed
reading.correct: That nobody will bring him a drink in the morning
reading.explain: He howls from the shed about the morning drink, and is told he will be fed according to the Geneva Convention.

highlight.question: Which sentence gives Tikhonov's opinion once the drink begins to wear off?
sentences: – А кто его знает!
Я, как выпью немножко, мне кажется, что хоть сегодня выступай, что и вчера было не рано выступать.
А как начинает проходить – нет, думаю, и вчера было рано, и послезавтра не поздно.
highlight.explain: The third sentence is the sober half of his answer: yesterday was too early and the day after tomorrow would not be too late.

highlight.question: Which sentence says where Venichka believes a revolution must happen if it is to achieve anything?
sentences: Тут я сразу должен оговориться, перед лицом совести всего человечества я должен сказать: я с самого начала был противником этой авантюры, бесплодной, как смоковница.
(Прекрасно сказано: «бесплодной, как смоковница».)
Я с самого начала говорил, что революция достигает чего-нибудь нужного, если совершается в сердцах, а не на стогнах.
Но уж раз начали без меня – я не мог быть в стороне от тех, кто начал.
Я мог бы, во всяком случае, предотвратить излишнее ожесточение сердец и ослабить кровопролитие…
highlight.explain: The third sentence contrasts revolution in hearts with revolution in the public squares.

highlight.question: Which sentence tells us where the answering half of the password comes from?
sentences: В девятом часу по Гринвичу, в траве у скотного двора, мы сидели и ждали.
Каждому, кто подходил, мы говорили: «Садись, товарищ, с нами – в ногах правды нет», и каждый оставался стоять, бряцал оружием и повторял условную фразу из Антонио Сальери: «Но правды нет и выше».
Шаловлив был этот пароль и двусмыслен, но нам было не до этого; приближалось девять ноль-ноль по Гринвичу…
highlight.explain: The second sentence names Antonio Salieri as the source of the reply the newcomers repeat.

highlight.question: Which sentence takes back the grand version of how the theses were put up?
sentences: С чего все началось?
Все началось с того, что Тихонов прибил к воротам елисейковского сельсовета свои четырнадцать тезисов.

Вернее, не прибил к воротам, а написал на заборе мелом, и это скорее были слова, а не тезисы, четкие и лапидарные слова, а не тезисы, и было их всего два, а не четырнадцать, – но, как бы то ни было, с этого все началось.
highlight.explain: The last sentence reduces fourteen nailed theses to two blunt words chalked on a fence.

highlight.question: Which sentence names the villages that begged for mercy?
sentences: Двумя колоннами, со штандартами в руках, мы вышли – колонна на Елисейково, другая – на Тартино.

И шли беспрепятственно, вплоть до заката: убитых не было ни с одной стороны, раненых тоже не было, пленный был только один – бывший председатель ларионовского сельсовета, на склоне лет разжалованный за пьянку и врожденное слабоумие.
Елисейково было повержено.
Черкасово валялось у нас в ногах, Неугодово и Пекша молили о пощаде.
Все жизненные центры петушинского уезда – от магазина в Поломах до андреевского склада сельпо, – все заняты были силами восставших…
highlight.explain: Neugodovo and Peksha are the two villages said to plead for mercy.

highlight.question: Which sentence describes what the four postcards looked like?
sentences: И послали четыре открытки: Аббе Эбану, Моше Даяну, генералу Сухарто и Александру Дубчеку.
Все четыре открытки были очень красивые, с виньеточками и желудями.
Пусть, мол, порадуются ребята, может они нас, губошлепы, признают за это субъектами международного права…
highlight.explain: The middle sentence describes the vignettes and acorns on the cards.
